observed_evidence: Reuters reported preliminary Kpler data showing only two commodity vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz on September 21, down from 10 a day earlier and versus roughly 125 large commercial vessels per day before the Iran conflict; AIS-dark crossings are not captured.

Marisks Intelligence reported that crude tanker LR Stephanie and LPG tanker Al Maryah were struck in separate Hormuz incidents; both continued without towing, responsibility was unconfirmed, and Reuters noted the relevant operators did not confirm attribution.

A senior Iranian official told Reuters Iran could reopen Hormuz within seven days if the United States eases military pressure and lifts its blockade on Iranian ports; this is a conditional diplomatic statement, not evidence that the strait has reopened.

Reuters sources reported Saudi Arabia restarted the East-West Pipeline at a low rate on September 22 after its September 13 shutdown. Aramco was seeking restoration toward 4 million bpd, while a security source said full resumption could take weeks.
semantic_interpretation: Physical Hormuz disruption remains extreme and direct vessel attacks raise shipping and insurance risk, while Iran's conditional diplomacy and Saudi Arabia's partial East-West Pipeline restart reduce the probability of the most severe sustained oil-export constraint. The signals are therefore mixed: near-term shipping risk escalated, but bypass capacity and diplomatic optionality improved.
